Fifteen years is the average lifespan of asphalt. Depending on the surface’s use and wear, it should be sealed every 2 years for protection. Asphalt is a major investment and an asset to your commercial or residential property. If it is kept in good condition, the asphalt will increase the value of your home or business and its appearance for many years to come.

We’re dedicated to you and your project, and strive to always provide the highest level of quality and care. We provide written and verbal communication throughout a project to keep clients informed. Our goal with every job is to exceed the client’s expectations and fulfill their needs.

Do I need asphalt maintenance and repairs? How can I tell?

There’s a variety of ways asphalt falls into disrepair. From alligator cracking to rutting, shoving to depressions, any number of issues may arise with your asphalt as time passes. You should schedule maintenance and repair service when cracks, holes or other signs of damage appear in the asphalt. If left without repair, these problems grow and become more costly to fix.

How long should I stay off freshly paved asphalt?

After having your driveway or parking lot paved with asphalt, you want to wait 72 hours before driving or walking on the surface. For roads, you can drive or walk on them as soon as the asphalt has compacted.

When should I seal my asphalt?

That all depends on the type of seal coating you want for your new asphalt. Six weeks after project completion, we can apply an oil-based sealing product. With latex sealer, you need to wait a full year before application.

Clients across West Palm Beach come to us for speed bump installation. Devices such as speed bumps, humps and tables allow you to maintain safe conditions in parking lots and on smaller roads. Depending on your needs and the space available, we can install bumps, humps or tables with ease.

Of course, we also repair any broken or deteriorated speed bumps, humps and tables.

Asphalt Paving Services
in West Palm Beach, FL

All American Asphalt LLC is a full-service paving contractor providing asphalt paving services in West Palm Beach, FL and serving throughout Plantation and Davie, FL. We specialize in all asphalt services, from overlays to asphalt sealing. Commercial and residential properties use asphalt for their parking lots, driveways, walking paths and smaller roadways. When property owners need paving, resurfacing or repair, they trust us to get the job done.
Call Now

West Palm Beach’s Choice for Asphalt Paving

Asphalt Repairs become necessary for a multitude of reasons. The first step in any asphalt repair project is identifying the cause of the asphalt damage. Sometimes this is obvious, such as when tree roots have broken through the surface, or when corrosive chemicals such as hydraulic fluid have eaten away at the asphalt. Other times poor drainage has left pools of standing water which can damage the asphalt over time.

View Gallery

When performing asphalt repairs, first a larger area around the pothole or depression is saw-cut and removed. If the exposed base rock underneath the asphalt needs to be addressed, now is the time to base up this areas to create an even surface for the patch. Next, a coat or tack, or asphalt emulsion, is applied to the surface to ensure asphalt adhesion. Hot mix asphalt is then installed and compacted to the correct thickness then a roller is used to create a smooth transition from the new patch to the surrounding asphalt.

Expert Asphalt Overlays and Repair

A new layer of asphalt can quickly and effectively return your parking lot or roadway to its original look. Adding thickness to your existing asphalt surfaces increases the structural integrity and adds a smooth and even finish. New asphalt can be paved directly on top of existing asphalt surfaces, and this is called an overlay. In addition, asphalt can be paved on top of a sufficient layer of compacted DOT-approved base rock. Areas that require full reconstruction can be excavated first prior to new base rock being installed.

View Gallery

The first step for any asphalt paving project is creating an ideal surface for the new asphalt. This may involve basing-up any low-lying areas or existing potholes with base rock, removing and setting aside any car stops, or cleaning the area of any detritus or debris. In addition, any transition areas may need to be milled down, and the current drainage structures may need to be adjusted to allow for the elevation change of the new layer of asphalt. Once the area has been suitably prepped, a layer of tack, or asphalt emulsion, is applied to the surface to ensure asphalt adhesion. Then, hot mix asphalt is applied in an even layer by an asphalt paving machine before being compacted with a vibratory steel-drum roller.

Asphalt Milling

Asphalt millings, also known as recycled asphalt pavement (RAP), come from previous asphalt projects that have been removed and crushed into gravel asphalt millings are cheaper and more eco-friendly than virgin asphalt, hence why more people are turning to this option, especially for residential construction. Depending on the nature of your project, asphalt millings can offer some unique benefits over traditional gravel or asphalt. That doesn’t mean it’s necessarily the right option for your project.

Striping is an essential part of any paving project, without which the project is not complete.

Road Work
